summary: A measured component is an object in an attester's target environment whose state can be sampled, usually hashed, such as firmware or loaded software. This Standards Track document provides an information model for it and two associated data models.

eli5.summary: A device writes fingerprints of its important parts to show nothing was swapped.

questions: how to represent firmware measurements in eat
subtitle: A common record for the fingerprint of one piece of firmware or software, ready to ride inside an Entity Attestation Token.

tldr.problem: The EAT Measurement claim only had one format, CoSWID tags, which cannot describe things that are not anchored to a file system, such as components in early boot.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 10013 defines a measured component: a name, an optional version, a digested or raw value, and optional signing authorities and flags. It gives one information model and two data models, CBOR and JSON, with media types and CoAP Content-Formats.
tldr.outcome: A measured component can be carried in the EAT Measurement claim alongside or instead of CoSWID. It is a Proposed Standard.

today: RFC 10013 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2026. It is not obsoleted or updated by any other RFC.

sections.title: The Gap in the EAT Measurement Claim
sections.content:
The Entity Attestation Token (RFC 9711) has a Measurement claim for describing the software or other measurable subsystems of an entity. Each measurement format is identified by a CoAP Content-Format. At the time of writing, the only specified format is a CoSWID tag of type evidence from RFC 9393.

CoSWID does not suit measurements that cannot be anchored to a file system, such as those in early boot environments. RFC 10013 fills that gap with a measured component format that can be used with the Measurement claim alongside or instead of CoSWID.

A measured component is an object in the attester's target environment whose state can be sampled and typically digested with a cryptographic hash. Examples are the invariant part of firmware loaded at startup, a Run-Time Integrity Check (RTIC), a file system object, or a CPU register.
sections.eli5: There was only one way to list what software a device runs, and it needed files. This RFC adds a way to list things that are not files, like the very first code a device runs when it wakes up.

sections.title: The Information Model
sections.content:
The RFC separates the idea from the encoding. The information model lists what a measured component contains. Two data models then implement it, and future specifications could add more, for example in ASN.1.

Each measured component has a Component Name (REQUIRED), which should stay the same across releases so the same item can be tracked across updates. It has an optional Component Version, where Semantic Versioning is RECOMMENDED. It has either a digested or a raw value (REQUIRED). The digest algorithm is REQUIRED only if the value is digested. Finally it may list Authorities, the entities that can authoritatively identify the component.

A data model implementing this SHOULD allow a limited amount of extensibility for profile-specific semantics.
sections.eli5: Each entry is like a label on a jar: the jar's name, maybe a version, and either a fingerprint of what is inside or the contents themselves.

sections.title: The measured-component Data Item
sections.content:
The data model is written in CDDL and works for both CBOR and JSON. It is inspired by the PSA software component claim in RFC 9783. The item is a map with these members:

  • id (index 1): the component identifier, a name and an optional version.
  • digested-measurement (index 2) or raw-measurement (index 5): exactly one of the two. The digested form is a digest, a pair of algorithm and value. The raw form is a byte string, whose size can vary greatly, so a decoder may limit the memory it allocates for it.
  • authorities (index 3): optional, one or more authority identifiers.
  • flags (index 4): optional, a 64-bit field.

The digest algorithm is an integer or a text string, interpreted against the IANA Named Information Hash Algorithm Registry. Integers match the ID entries and text matches the Hash Name String entries. Using the integer is RECOMMENDED where possible.
sections.eli5: The record is a small form with numbered boxes. Box 1 is the name, box 2 is the fingerprint, and the other boxes are optional extras.

sections.title: Authorities and Profile-Specific Flags
sections.content:
An authority is an entity that can authoritatively identify a component by digitally signing it. The signature is typically checked at installation, or when the boot firmware, operating system or application launcher runs the component, as in UEFI Secure Boot and Arm Trusted Board Boot. An authority is identified by its signing public key, which could be an X.509 certificate, a raw public key, a thumbprint, or another identifier. This signature is unrelated to the attester's signature on the EAT itself.

The flags field carries up to 64 bits of profile-defined meaning and is exactly 8 bytes. If an EAT profile uses measured components, it MUST say whether it uses the authorities field and the flags field, and how to interpret them.

If the consumer does not know the EAT profile and a measured component includes authorities or flags, the consumer MUST reject the EAT.
sections.eli5: An authority is whoever signed the part, like the maker's stamp. The flags box is a small set of switches whose meaning is set by the rulebook of the particular system.

sections.title: Carrying Components in an EAT
sections.content:
The RFC extends the EAT $measurements-body-cbor and $measurements-body-json sockets. Each gets two new forms. The homogeneous form is used when the measured component and the EAT use the same serialization. The tunnel form is used when they differ, and the CoAP Content-Format then describes the original serialization.

Two media types are registered: application/measured-component+cbor and application/measured-component+json. IANA registered the matching CoAP Content-Format IDs 295 and 296.

The examples describe a boot loader with a sha-256 digest, a version 1.2.3rc2, two authorities and flags, and a raw component named hardware-config.
sections.eli5: If a box and its contents are both in the same language, hand it over as is. If not, wrap it in a labeled envelope that says which language it is in.

sections.title: Security and Privacy Considerations
sections.content:
The EAT considerations on claim trustworthiness, multiple EAT consumers and detached bundle digests also apply here. The component name and version can give an attacker detailed insight into the software and configuration on a device, and may reveal private information about the device and its owner. The stability requirement on the name may also enable tracking.

Text fields stored in files, inserted into databases or shown to humans must be properly sanitized. A digested measurement must use a strong cryptographic hash function.
sections.eli5: A label that names exactly what is inside can also tell a burglar what to look for, so the names need care.
